modules.role: the USB end: the Type-C receptacle, its 10uF VBUS reservoir and the VBUS lamp; the two 5.1k CC pulldowns are their own termination island so the connector keeps room for the mirrored D+/D- pin pairs
the two CC pulldowns: 5.1k from CC1 and CC2 to GND, the pair a sink must present for the host to enumerate; both are shunt branches to the same ground flag
the bridge: CH343G alone, with VDD5, V3, VIO, USB data and the UART/MODEM pins leaving as flags or labels; its decoupling lives in the adjacent ch343_power island
the bridge supply decoupling: C1 100nF on VDD5, C3 100nF on the V3 regulator output, C4 100nF on the VCC/VIO level rail; each is a shunt from a rail to GND
the far end: the 2x5P 2.54mm header carrying the eight UART/MODEM lines plus the VCC level rail and GND, where the peer board attaches

directWiringObligations.note: the VBUS lamp's cathode and R3 are one conductor inside the usb_c island: labelPolicy.local is 'wire', so naming the lamp's return would be a label where the policy promises a wire (534; the pair is D1 pin 2 to R3 pin 1, nothing else on the net)

localLabelObligations.note: Type-C 可逆引脚交错: the receptacle's data pins are mirrored pairs, D+ on USB1.A6/B6 and D- on USB1.A7/B7, so one wire inside usb_c would have to tie the two halves of a pair and draw a U-line that presents one pin as the other; instead each of the four pins takes its own short stub and the golden board's same-name label (D+ on A6 and B6, D- on A7 and B7), and the pair reaches U1.5/U1.6 by the same-named labels there — the name carries the net, no U-line does
